candidates.label: bc2 (timing-neutral bodycell hook cells)
candidates.change: A: push cs/pop es -> les di,[si+arenaptr] (dw 0,1000h: ES=arena, DI=0 as before); freed slot = lea cx,[si+cellA]; after mov [9769h],ax add mov [si+cellA],ax; mov cx,4A17h removed. zom20a is hooked as jmp [cellA]. B: push cs/pop es -> les di,[si+arenaptr]; add mov [si+cellB],bx; mov cx,4A17h -> lea cx,[si+cellB]; after cld self-patch zombie_entry's mov cx imm16 to cellB; band math mov ah,al/add ah,10h/mov al,0A2h -> xchg al,ah/add ax,10A2h (same AX incl. wrap). Timing vs rev0 unchanged: A reads [4A17h] instr 4, writes [9769h] instr 5, INT87 instr 10, phoenix turn 22; B writes [4A17h] instr 3, [5D13h] instr 5, INT87 instr 12, phoenix turn 25. Zombie paths unchanged except the patched hook cell.
candidates.groupNotes: Screen y6bql vs rev0: cand 0.6356 base 0.6456, ALL -0.0101 [-0.0190,-0.0012] 9/19; 2025 -0.0084; strong -0.0222 [-0.0371,-0.0074] 0/5; threat -0.0080; multi -0.0042. Same-layout control bc2ctl (t2n39) gives ALL -0.0110, so paired bc2 minus bc2ctl (computed per cohort from the two screens) = +0.0009 +-0.0041 4/4 (2025 +0.0013, strong -0.0048, threat +0.0035, multi -0.0042). The defense itself costs nothing measurable; the -0.010 comes from the shared layout (les and in-body stores, longer non-CC body). Size alone does not: pad control ufzyj = 0.0000. Threat reu4e (1 copy, 4 cohorts x 20 battles each): ALL +0.0623 [0.0244,0.1003] 14/3; B073poison +0.194 [0.082,0.306] 4/0 (poisoner team 0.6375 vs base, 0.500 vs bc2); B083poisonE +0.119 [0.072,0.165] 4/0 (0.610 vs base, 0.498 vs bc2); B073ctl -0.0125 [-0.037,0.012]; lead_V6 +0.025 [-0.003,0.053]; lead_V4 +0.059 [-0.015,0.134]; lead_V6Guard -0.010 [-0.061,0.040].

candidates.label: bc2ctl (layout control, defense off)
candidates.change: bc2 with lea cx,[si+cellX] replaced by lea cx,[4A17h] in A and B (4-byte encoding; same size, same instruction count). Hooks use [4A17h] as in rev0; the zcx self-patch rewrites 4A17h. 3 bytes differ per warrior from bc2.

candidates.label: pad (placement control)
candidates.change: rev0 A + 13 CCh bytes, rev0 B + 15 CCh bytes at the end (sizes = bc2). Code bytes identical to rev0.
candidates.groupNotes: Only 2 of 50 cohorts changed (s2025-12 +0.033, Baltika9 -0.033). Body size alone (+13/+15 bytes) does not change placement or outcomes.

candidates.label: B083poisonE (counter-code, test case)
candidates.change: B073 poisoner (MOVSW twin of rev0, own cell 7B2Dh) with the B write mov [4A17h],bx done at instr 3 AND instr 4 (push cs/pop es -> les di to keep its INT87 at instr 12; own-cell write moves to instr 6, so its A copies a stale value to [9769h]; harmless for its own capture). It wins A's 1-round [4A17h] channel (our B writes round 3, our A reads round 4) in either round order. A = B073 counterA.
candidates.groupNotes: reu4e: poisonE team 0.610 vs base (ctl twin 0.494), 0.498 vs bc2; bc2 minus base +0.119 vs poisonE (B073 poisoner: +0.194).

threatFindings.threat: A fixed-cell [4A17h] poisoner (one write at instr 5) takes the base's captured Zombies.
threatFindings.evidence: reu4e: poisoner team 0.6375 vs base against 0.494 for the plain twin ctl; bc2 (cells in own bodies) recovers +0.194 [0.082,0.306] 4/0 against it; replicates B073 9xz3y/j77yv.
threatFindings.impact: About -0.1 to -0.2 per battle for the base against one poisoner in its cohorts; no archived team does this (only the V6 family writes [4A17h]).

threatFindings.threat: Early poisoner (writes [4A17h] at instr 3 and 4) also takes the base's Zombies, and still poisons the A channel of a bodycell fix (A's zom20a hook cell gets the poisoner's entry).
threatFindings.evidence: reu4e: poisonE team 0.610 vs base; bc2 gains +0.119 [0.072,0.165] 4/0 against it, versus +0.194 against the instr-5 poisoner.
threatFindings.impact: bc2 keeps the b/d chain safe against any cell writer. Against poisonE only part of the protection remains (the zom20a capture still leaks).

threatFindings.threat: Residual A-channel leak is significant (bc2 protects less against poisonE than against the instr-5 poisoner).
threatFindings.evidence: +0.119 vs +0.194, n=4 cohorts each, intervals overlap; poisonE team score vs bc2 (0.498) equals the twin's level (0.506). Not traced.
threatFindings.impact: If real, roughly -0.07 per battle in poisonE cohorts. Closing it needs a team-private channel (team-shared memory at the initial ES, DS switching because segment prefixes are invalid; about 4 extra A instructions before INT 87h).

threatFindings.threat: Moving the hook cells into our own bodies has a general field cost.
threatFindings.evidence: bc2 minus bc2ctl (same size, same timing, only the hook cell differs), paired per cohort from y6bql and t2n39: +0.0009 +-0.0041, W/L 4/4; strong -0.0048 +-0.0094.
threatFindings.impact: None measurable on field S. The defense itself is free.

threatFindings.threat: The bc2 layout (les di instead of push cs/pop es, in-body cell stores and data, longer non-CC body) costs on the general field.
threatFindings.evidence: Both bc2 (y6bql -0.0101 [-0.0190,-0.0012]) and bc2ctl (t2n39 -0.0110 [-0.0192,-0.0028]) lose; strong group 0/5 in both; size-only pad control ufzyj = 0.0000. The two screens share most cohort results, so they are not independent replications.
threatFindings.impact: About -0.01 per battle on field S, concentrated on s2025-10 (OpcodeHunter cohort, -0.122) and the strong group. Which byte change causes it (les encoding, extra stores, data words read by searchers) is a hypothesis; untraced.

threatFindings.threat: Size alone (+13/+15 bytes) changes placements and outcomes.
threatFindings.evidence: ufzyj: rev0 padded with CCh to bc2 sizes, ALL 0.0000, 1/1 changed cohorts.
threatFindings.impact: Byte-count growth is not a cost by itself; code-content changes are.

threatFindings.threat: Sharing [4A17h] with the V6 family costs the base (their B writes [4A17h] in the same round 3).
A write to [5D13h] or [9769h] redirects our own Zombies.
threatFindings.evidence: Static: neither rev0 nor bc2 hooks through these cells (they are theft cells only); the poisoners take Zombies through [4A17h] alone.

recommendation: Do not promote bc2 alone (screen ALL -0.010). But the defense part is free: against a same-size, same-timing control it scores +0.001 +-0.004 on field S, and it removes most of the fixed-cell theft (+0.19 vs the B073 poisoner, +0.12 vs the early poisoner, 4/0 each, 1 copy). The -0.010 comes from the bytes and layout that pay for the timing neutrality (les di, in-body stores/data), not from body size (pad = 0). Suggestion for a combination wave: port the hook-cell change onto a base whose startup is already rebuilt (for example C2-A's 16-bit band math frees 3 A turns, so lea cx/mov [si+cellA] can be added without les). Then screen it against a same-layout defense-off control, as here, so the defense effect is separated from layout noise. Add B073poison and B083poisonE to the threat library.
notes: Same-layout controls are the right way to screen small defensive edits: bc2 and bc2ctl differ in 3 bytes per warrior and differ from each other in only 8/50 cohorts, while each differs from rev0 in 26-28 cohorts.
